messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: P2 alert from runtime-cluster-3: OOM on gpu-node-3-12 while serving /v1/generate. Paging sam_oncall.
sam_oncall: I'm on it, starting bridge -> https://zoom.redwood/bridge/1758002468 :phone: joining now
nina_runtime: seen the alert, pulling telemetry. stacktraces show `cudaMalloc` failures and repeated `KVCache::grow()` spikes.
nina_runtime: quick peek at gpu stats (from metrics-agent): GPU3 memory: total 48Gi, used 47.2Gi, fragmentation ~18%, biggest free chunk 120Mi. per-process RSS: 43.8Gi
raj_ml: customer impact? which models / customers hit?
kevin_support: support: we're seeing 5 support tickets flagged for low-qps customers on us-east-1, but two enterprise customers reported increased 5xx/timeout.
lisa_acctmgr: flagged account: acme-ads. They're ondedicated? No, hosted. Asking for timeline for exec update.
clara_sre: hypothesis 1: KV cache growth + large batch sizes triggering fragmentation and OOM on allocations for new KV pages. hypothesis 2: kernel memory leak in attention kernel allocation path.
sam_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) divert traffic off gpu-node-3-12, 2) lower batching for us-east pool to batch_size=1 for suspect models, 3) enable model-variant fallback to cpu-quant for heavy requests, 4) consider kvcache eviction sweep.
nina_runtime: action: scaling down batch size via runtime config. running:
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood/runtime/config" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"pool":"us-east-prod","batch_limit":1}'
```
nina_runtime: also toggled `KV_CACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.65` on gpu-pool-3 to force earlier eviction.
clara_sre: I'm running a live memory map dump on the node:
```
ssh gpu-node-3-12 sudo /opt/redwood/bin/gpu-mem-dump --pid 4123 --out /tmp/memdump-1758002468.log
```
clara_sre: shared /tmp/memdump-1758002468.log to #eng-runtime (link in bridge). Contains top allocators: kvcache shards, attention_kv_buffer, batch_workspace
raj_ml: from logs: large requests pattern: many concurrent short-chat calls with long prefix leading to big KV footprints. Suggest rate-limit per-session, or force prefix-truncation at 8k tokens for now.
kevin_support: posted customer impact notes to incident ticket: acme-ads saw 12 failed requests in 12m window, fallback to cpu-quant successful for 9 of them, 3 remain errors. ops noted higher latency.
sam_oncall: timeline so far (local): 12:01 alert -> 12:03 pager -> 12:05 divert traffic off node -> 12:07 batch_size=1 applied -> 12:10 KV evict threshold raised -> 12:12 partial recovery signals. still seeing occasional OOMs on node.
clara_sre: collecting heap traces next. if OOMs persist after kv eviction, we'll do a graceful process restart for the worker and rotate the node out of the pool.
nina_runtime: quick metric dump: kvcache size growth last 30m: +28%, eviction rate flat at 0.02 ops/s -> indicates eviction policy stuck. suspect a GC bug for pinned prefixes.
raj_ml: hypothesis: a small set of sessions (chatbots) pin prefixes with long conv histories that never age out due to a bug in last-access timestamp update. That prevents eviction and fragments GPU heap.
sam_oncall: short-term: continue routing heavy customers to fallback pool; SRE to run eviction script; Runtime to patch timestamp update in next hotfix if root cause confirmed. Who owns hotfix?
nina_runtime: I can assemble a minimal patch for timestamp-update logic, test on staging, and push a canary to dedicated-2. ETA 90m for canary PR if no blockers.
clara_sre: I'll run eviction sweep now: `/opt/redwood/bin/kv-evict --pool=us-east-prod --age=2h --force` and monitor OOMs.
clara_sre: eviction sweep started at 12:18, posted logs to bridge. linking snippet: `evicted 4.2Gi from 128 shards`.
kevin_support: update for acme-ads: routed 70% traffic to cpu-fallback, support message queued to explain mitigation and ETA.
lisa_acctmgr: thanks team. I'll draft an exec note: caused by KV pinning/eviction gap, mitigated by traffic routing + eviction sweep, hotfix in progress, will update in 2 hours.
sam_oncall: good. keep this thread for RCA notes. please paste final timeline + logs here for postmortem. :thumbsup:
nina_runtime: saving memdumps and eviction logs to s3://redwood-incidents/1758002468/ for RCA. will attach stack traces and PR link.
clara_sre: marking incident as in-progress -> mitigation underway. will reopen if OOMs reappear after evict and restart.
kevin_support: closing loop with customers: acme-ads notified, support ticket updated with mitigation steps and temporary SLA impact note.
sam_oncall: end-of-bridge checklist: capture timeline, attach memdumps, list hypotheses (kv pinning, attention alloc leak), owner for hotfix (nina_runtime), SRE follow-up (clara_sre). will create postmortem doc after logs validated.
